title: Elmina Castle
summary: Elmina Castle (São Jorge da Mina), on the coast of present-day Ghana, was built by the Portuguese in 1482 to trade in gold. Taken by the Dutch in 1637 and ceded to Britain in 1872, it later became a main centre of the transatlantic slave trade. It is part of a UNESCO World Heritage site.

uncertainty.note: Start is the Portuguese construction date; end is the 1872 cession to Britain, the last transfer between European powers (the castle still stands).

as_recorded.value: Erected by the Portuguese in 1482 (Diogo de Azambuja)
Captured by the Dutch in 1637. Ceded to the British in 1872.

where.historical_name: Castelo de São Jorge da Mina (Portuguese, 1482); Elmina Castle under the Dutch (1637-1872); Gold Coast fortress

importance.justification: Oldest European building in sub-Saharan Africa, first a gold-trade post and later a major node of the transatlantic slave trade.

audience_note: Concerns a fortress used in the transatlantic slave trade.
